chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us from 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Abu Ahmad al-Azdi, from 'Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Abu 'Umar al-'Ajami, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

God — Mighty and Majestic is His glory — said: I am God; there is no god but Me. I created the kings, and their hearts are in My hand. Whenever a people obey Me, I make the hearts of the kings toward them [full of] mercy. And whenever a people disobey Me, I make the hearts of the kings toward them [full of] wrath. Behold! Do not busy yourselves with insulting the kings — repent to Me, and I will incline their hearts toward you.

key_terms.جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ: An honorific formula meaning 'Mighty and Majestic is His glory', expressing God's transcendent majesty
key_terms.حَدِيثٌ قُدْسِيٌّ: Divine Hadith — a narration in which the Prophet transmits words spoken directly by God, distinct from the Quran
key_terms.سَخَطَةٌ: Divine wrath or displeasure; here expressing kings' harshness toward a disobedient people
key_terms.قُلُوبُ الْمُلُوكِ بِيَدِي: 'The hearts of the kings are in My hand' — an anthropomorphic expression indicating God's absolute control over rulers' dispositions

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the relationship between a people's obedience to God and their rulers' treatment of them?
ai.summary: This is a Divine Hadith (hadith qudsi) in which God addresses the relationship between a community's obedience and the dispositions of their rulers. The hadith teaches that political hardship is a consequence of collective disobedience, and its remedy is repentance rather than blaming rulers. Transmitted through Imam 'Ali and the Prophet, this teaching was especially meaningful during periods of political oppression, redirecting communal frustration from external grievance toward internal spiritual reform.
